SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
PUC DOCKET NO. 59475

INTERVENOR NELDA HOWTON'S LIMITED EXCEPTIONS TO THE PROPOSAL FOR DECISION
(Limited to the Conditional Selection of Route 894)
TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES AND THE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS:
Intervenor Nelda Howton, appearing pro se, respectfully submits these Limited Exceptions to the Proposal for Decision ("PFD") issued August 20, 2026. These Exceptions are intentionally narrow.
Mrs. Howton agrees with and supports the PFD's principal determination and ultimate recommendation that the Joint Application should be denied. Her primary position is that the Central Texas pathway should not be completed at all and that the Application now before the Commission should be denied in full. She therefore asks the Commission to adopt the PFD's recommendation of denial.
Mrs. Howton files an exception only to the PFD's alternative or conditional routing recommendation that, if the Commission determines the project should nevertheless be approved, Route 894 should be selected. PFD at 147-48. If the Commission departs from the PFD's recommendation of denial and authorizes this project, Mrs. Howton respectfully requests that Route 296 be selected instead of Route 894 and that no approved route include Link F20.
This filing does not ask the Commission to reconsider the PFD's favorable findings supporting denial. It preserves Mrs. Howton's prior route-specific objections and explains why the same record that supports denial also does not support Route 894 as the fallback route.
PRIMARY POSITION: Mrs. Howton agrees with SOAH and asks the Commission to deny the Application in full. Her position is that the Central Texas pathway should not be completed at all; the relief available in this docket is denial of this Application.
ALTERNATIVE POSITION ONLY IF THE COMMISSION APPROVES THE PROJECT: Route 894 should be rejected and Route 296 should be selected instead. No approved route should include Link F20.
I. MRS. HOWTON AGREES WITH THE PFD THAT THE APPLICATION SHOULD BE DENIED
The PFD concludes that Applicants did not establish that amendment of their certificates is necessary for the service, accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public and recommends that the Bell County East-to-Big Hill project not be approved. Mrs. Howton agrees with that conclusion.
The PFD also concludes that the Application should be denied because Applicants failed to provide the public-meeting process required for approximately 1,400 landowners affected by newly added route segments. Mrs. Howton agrees that this notice failure was material and that denial is the appropriate remedy.
Accordingly, Mrs. Howton's first and preferred relief is simple: adopt the PFD's recommendation and deny the Application. Nothing below should be read as support for construction of the Central Texas pathway. The Route 296 discussion is presented only as an alternative in the event the Commission rejects the PFD's recommended denial.
II. LIMITED EXCEPTION: ROUTE 894 SHOULD NOT BE THE FALLBACK ROUTE
The PFD describes its routing task as choosing the "least bad option" if a route must be selected and conditionally recommends Route 894. Mrs. Howton respectfully excepts to that portion of the PFD. Route 894 uses Link F20, and the record contains specific, unresolved defects concerning F20 that prevent Route 894 from being the best-supported alternative.
A. The notice failure that supports denial also undermines the Route 894/F20 record.
Mrs. Howton's prior filings repeatedly explained that landowners affected by later-added alternate links did not receive the same meaningful opportunity as originally noticed landowners to investigate the proposed route, review Applicants' environmental counts, identify errors, retain counsel or experts, coordinate with neighboring landowners, and participate while routes and links were still being shaped.
Her Proposed Findings specifically stated that the compressed notice period was not harmless because the record later revealed discrepancies in F20 data involving habitable structures, cultural resources, environmental information, and community values. Nelda Howton Proposed Findings of Fact Nos. 33-34 (June 26, 2026).
The PFD's own notice ruling confirms the seriousness of this procedural problem. It would be inconsistent to recognize that later-added landowners were deprived of the required public-meeting process, yet rely on the resulting incomplete F20 record to select Route 894 as the fallback route. 
B. The F20 habitable-structure count was not adequately field-verified and was shown to be inaccurate.
Applicants relied primarily on desktop review, aerial photography, GIS information, and route-wide tables in evaluating F20. The record does not show adequate boots-on-the-ground verification before F20 was used in Route 894. Hearing Tr. Vol. 2 at 120:18-124:8, PUC Interchange Item No. 6137.
Cross-examination then identified the Carl Simpson residence approximately 383 feet from Link F20, within the 500-foot habitable-structure distance. Applicants' witness acknowledged that the residence appeared to be within that distance and that the F20 count would be adjusted if the structure met Applicants' habitable-structure standard. Hearing Tr. Vol. 4 at 51:8-52:21, 52:15-21, PUC Interchange Item No. 6137.
Mrs. Howton had already challenged the F20 count as understated. The hearing testimony independently confirmed that at least one residence had not been reliably accounted for. A route-wide comparison cannot fairly treat Route 894's reported habitable-structure number as an advantage when the underlying F20 count was shown to be incomplete or disputed. Prudent avoidance depends on accurate identification of homes, not unverified numbers in a desktop table.
C. Route 894/F20 does not adequately account for First Cedar Valley Baptist Church or local cultural and historical values.
First Cedar Valley Baptist Church is a longstanding Cedar Valley church and community landmark near Link F20. The record identifies the church as established in or about 1942 and located approximately 690 to 720 feet from the F20 centerline. The church is directly relevant to community values, historical values, aesthetic values, and cultural-resource considerations.
Mrs. Howton's prior briefing explained that Applicants' F20 analysis did not adequately reflect this church in the cultural-resource evaluation. A generalized methodology is not reliable when it omits a known community landmark within the review area. See Nelda Howton Reply to Initial Post-Hearing Briefs at 8; PUC Interchange Item No. 5925; Hearing Tr. Vol. 2 at 117:8-119:8, PUC Interchange Item No. 6137.
That omission weighs against Route 894 and in favor of a route, such as Route 296, that avoids the localized F20 impacts identified in the record.
D. The F20 environmental and endangered-species analysis was not adequately field-verified.
The record contains unresolved Golden-cheeked Warbler habitat concerns near F20. Applicants' witness confirmed that no site-specific Golden-cheeked Warbler habitat field survey was conducted on Link F20 before route selection and that the F20 endangered-species figure was based on GIS/U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service mapping rather than field verification. Hearing Tr. Vol. 4 at 52:23-54:8, PUC Interchange Item No. 6137.
Mrs. Howton's Proposed Findings therefore stated that Applicants had not provided comparable F20-specific U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service validation before recommending a route using F20. Nelda Howton Proposed Findings of Fact Nos. 20-23.
Post-approval surveys or later agency coordination do not cure the route-selection problem. The Commission must compare routes on the record before it permanently selects a corridor. Unverified assumptions concerning F20 should not be treated as an advantage over Route 296.
E. Buttermilk Creek presents unresolved historical, archaeological, and cultural-resource concerns.
Mrs. Howton's prior findings and briefing identify unresolved historical, archaeological, and cultural-resource concerns in the Buttermilk Creek drainage near F20. The record indicates that F20 crosses or approaches areas of high archaeological potential and that Applicants did not field-survey those areas before selecting F20.
Route-wide cultural-resource tables should not be treated as conclusive where the record identifies an unsurveyed sensitive drainage area together with a nearby longstanding church and community landmark. These link-specific concerns weigh against Route 894.
F. The Cedar Valley tornado and continuing recovery were omitted from the Environmental Assessment.
The April 12, 2022 EF-3 tornado through Cedar Valley is a material community-value consideration. Cross-examination confirmed that Applicants' Environmental Assessment did not reference that tornado. Hearing Tr. Vol. 4 at 54:10-14, PUC Interchange Item No. 6137.
Applicants' witness also confirmed that the routing criteria did not contain a specific criterion for a corridor recovering from a declared natural disaster or for post-disaster recovery. Hearing Tr. Vol. 4 at 55:4-23, PUC Interchange Item No. 6137.
The fact that Applicants' table lacked a disaster-recovery category does not make the existing community burden irrelevant. The Commission's statutory consideration of community values requires meaningful attention to the actual conditions on the ground. The continuing recovery of Cedar Valley therefore weighs against imposing the additional permanent burden of Link F20.
III. IF THE COMMISSION APPROVES THE PROJECT DESPITE THE PFD, ROUTE 296 SHOULD BE SELECTED
Route 296 is not merely Mrs. Howton's preference; it is a record-supported alternative that avoids Link F20 and the specific F20 defects described above. Mrs. Howton consistently supported Route 296 in her Initial Post-Hearing Brief, Reply Brief, and Proposed Findings.
Commission Staff witness John Poole confirmed that Route 296 was his second-place route and ranked above Applicants' Route 894. Hearing Tr. Vol. 4 at 91:21-92:4, PUC Interchange Item No. 6137. Mrs. Howton's Proposed Findings therefore expressly requested Route 296 as the preferred non-F20 route. Nelda Howton Proposed Findings of Fact Nos. 35-36; Conclusions of Law Nos. 12-13.
The objections raised against Route 296 do not cure the defects in F20. Route selection is not a binary exercise in which criticism of Route 296 automatically validates Route 894. The Commission must compare the reliability of the underlying evidence. Here, the F20 record contains demonstrated notice problems, a disputed habitable-structure count, inadequate field verification, omitted community and cultural resources, unresolved endangered-species and archaeological concerns, and an unaddressed disaster-recovery burden.
For those reasons, if the Commission determines that a route must be approved notwithstanding the PFD's recommendation of denial, Route 296 is the better-supported alternative and should be selected instead of Route 894.
IV. REQUESTED MODIFICATION TO THE PFD
Mrs. Howton respectfully requests that the PFD be adopted with the following limited modification:
1. Adopt the PFD's recommendation that the Joint Application be denied and that the proposed Central Texas pathway / Import Path 2 project at issue in this docket not be approved.
2. If the Commission determines otherwise and approves the project, reject the PFD's conditional recommendation of Route 894.
3. Find that the record does not support selection of Route 894 or any route using Link F20 because the F20 analysis is materially incomplete or unreliable with respect to notice, habitable structures, environmental and endangered-species habitat, community values, cultural and historical resources, archaeological sensitivity, and disaster recovery.
4. If a route must be approved, select Route 296 as the route supported by the record and preferred by Mrs. Howton.
5. Modify the proposed findings, conclusions, and ordering paragraphs as necessary to reflect this relief.
V. CONCLUSION AND PRAYER
Mrs. Howton agrees with SOAH that the Application should be denied. Her primary request is that the Commission adopt that recommendation and decline to authorize construction of the Central Texas pathway at issue in this docket.
Her only exception is to the PFD's fallback selection of Route 894. If the Commission nevertheless authorizes the project, the Commission should not impose Route 894 and Link F20 on a record containing the specific defects established in Mrs. Howton's prior submissions and at the hearing. Route 296 should be selected instead.
Mrs. Howton respectfully requests all other relief to which she may be justly entitled.
Respectfully submitted,
/s/ Nelda Howton
Nelda Howton
Pro Se Intervenor
Party No. 250
12600 FM 2843
Salado, Texas 76571
